title: Sardine can
prompt: A labelled teaching model of the page 32 key-opening sardine can has a metal sealing band around its perimeter and a matching winding key. Fit key captures the band's tab. Turn key winds the removed band onto the narrow key shaft and releases the seal. Lift lid removes the freed lid. See-through shows the key handle and shaft, tab, remaining band, wound band, can body and lid. Opening permanently separates the specimen. Any specimen replacement is a teaching reset, not self-repair.
blurb: A staged teaching model winds a sacrificial sealing band onto its key, then lifts the freed lid; replacement supplies a new sealed can.
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / The Wheel and Axle

identity.note: The Wheel and Axle at Work / Sardine Can, page 32. The pictured key winds a metal sealing band from around the can.
identity.mechanism: The key handle applies torque to its narrow shaft, pulling and winding the sealing band away from the can.
identity.classificationNote: Only The Wheel and Axle and Gears and Belts are main principle chapters in this unit. Other entries are named examples, diagrams or subsection headings. Greek Mill has both historical context and a named mechanism diagram.

adaptationDecision.reason: Retain. Prior can-opener uses a cutting wheel at the rim, bottle-opener levers off a cap, and corkscrew extracts a cork with a helix and gears. These do not cover winding a sacrificial sealing band.
adaptationDecision.boundary: Catalog and figure metadata establish intended scope only. No existing figure runtime was certified.

prompt.note: Key opening is supported. Specify the perimeter sealing band pictured, not a modern pull-tab lid or a cut made by an added can-opener wheel. Unroll can inspect waste but must not imply that unwinding reseals the can. A lid-removal action is clearer.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Named machine example with staged specimen handling. It reproduces the supported key-and-band mechanism rather than adding a cutter.

builderTruthNotes: Simple tool and specimen. Label key handle, shaft, tab, band, lid and body. Do not invent internal machinery.

Label all meaningful drawn real components and physical features. Distinguish force and travel overlays from anatomy. The individual builder brief must declare its expected minimum before building. No invented parts to meet a quota.
Identify the teaching adaptation in metadata, blurb and truth notes. Reset, specimen exchange, slow view and hand positioning are teaching controls rather than hidden machine hardware.

teachingAdaptations: Opening is slowed and divided into four quarter-perimeter turns.
Replace specimen discards the opened can and wound waste and supplies a new sealed can; it does not reseal metal.
Thickness and the tab are enlarged for legibility.
See-through fades the can, lid and wound coil to expose the captured tab and same shaft; no hidden machinery is added.
truthNotes: The same key shaft captures the tab and carries all wound band.
Removed length increases monotonically; remaining plus wound perimeter length is constant.
Coil radius squared increases by removed length times metal thickness divided by pi.
The lid cannot lift while any sealing band remains.
The 1988 edition remains inaccessible and unverified. No edition-union claim is made.
